statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-4046 (GLIBC-SA-2026-0007) is in the IBM1390 and IBM1399 converters of the GNU C Library (glibc), which glibc ships as its IBM1390.so and IBM1399.so iconv modules: iconv() in glibc 2.43 and earlier can abort on an assertion failure when converting input from those character sets, crashing the calling program. https://sourceware.org/git/?p=glibc.git;a=blob_plain;f=advisories/GLIBC-SA-2026-0007, fixed by https://sourceware.org/git/?p=glibc.git;a=commit;h=d6f08d1cf027f4eb2ba289a6cc66853722d4badc; https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-4046 (fixed for trixie in glibc 2.41-12+deb13u3). This package does not contain glibc. Unpacked all 51 binary packages published from the curl source in the DHI Debian repository: curl 8.14.1 in its three published Debian revisions, built from Debian's 8.14.1-2+deb13u5 and 8.14.1-2+deb13u7 sources, for amd64 and arm64, namely curl, libcurl4t64, libcurl3t64-gnutls, libcurl4-openssl-dev, libcurl4-gnutls-dev and libcurl4-doc, and the debug-symbol packages curl-dbgsym, libcurl4t64-dbgsym and libcurl3t64-gnutls-dbgsym. Their ELF files are the curl program and the libcurl.so.4.8.0 (OpenSSL) and libcurl-gnutls.so.4.8.0 (GnuTLS) shared libraries, each dynamically linked against the system libc.so.6, plus detached debug-information files in the debug-symbol packages. The development packages also ship the static archives libcurl.a and libcurl-gnutls.a, each with 179 members that are all libcurl's own object files. No package contains a PE or Mach-O file. None of the packages contains libc.so.6, the dynamic loader, libc.a, a glibc gconv module or any other copy of glibc, and no archive member is a C library object. glibc reaches an image only through the separate libc6 package built from the glibc source, which is not part of this owner and is assessed on its own.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-4046 (GLIBC-SA-2026-0007, glibc bug 33980): iconv() in the GNU C Library 2.43 and earlier could abort on an assertion failure when converting input from the IBM1390 or IBM1399 character sets, so untrusted input could crash the calling program. https://sourceware.org/git/?p=glibc.git;a=blob_plain;f=advisories/GLIBC-SA-2026-0007. Upstream fixed it on the 2.41 branch in https://sourceware.org/git/?p=glibc.git;a=commit;h=61737f43b1f0d9f64a6f16649625476b70f9f4d3 (master: d6f08d1cf027f4eb2ba289a6cc66853722d4badc). Debian fixed it for trixie in 2.41-12+deb13u3 (DLA-4621-1 for bullseye, Debian bug 1132499, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-4046). The one glibc build published in the DHI Debian repository is Debian's 2.41-12+deb13u4 rebuilt for DHI, on amd64 and arm64; the version banner in its libc.so.6 names that Debian release (glibc 2.41). We checked the libc6 package of that build for both architectures against the repository index checksum: the Debian changelog it ships carries the 2.41-12+deb13u3 entry that applies the upstream stable-branch fix for CVE-2026-4046. The range ends at that build.

statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-4046 (GLIBC-SA-2026-0007) is in the IBM1390 and IBM1399 converters of the GNU C Library (glibc), versions 2.43 and earlier: iconv can hit an assertion failure and abort the calling program when converting crafted input from those character sets. Debian fixed it in trixie in glibc 2.41-12+deb13u3. https://sourceware.org/git/?p=glibc.git;a=blob_plain;f=advisories/GLIBC-SA-2026-0007, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-4046. This package does not contain glibc. Unpacked every binary package published from the ncurses source in the DHI Debian repository for amd64 and arm64 (56 index entries in 50 distinct files, because the architecture-independent ncurses-base, ncurses-term and ncurses-doc are listed for both): both published rebuilds of Debian's ncurses 6.5+20250216-2 (libtinfo6, libncurses6, libncursesw6, libncurses-dev, ncurses-bin, ncurses-base, ncurses-term, ncurses-doc and ncurses-examples, and the debug-symbol packages for libtinfo6, libncurses6, libncursesw6, ncurses-bin and ncurses-examples). None of them contains libc.so.6, the dynamic loader, libc.a, libpthread or another glibc library, a glibc gconv module, the glibc version banner, a statically linked program, a PE or Mach-O file, or a jar, whl, zip or nupkg archive. The shared libraries (libtinfo, libtic, libncurses, libncursesw, libform, libformw, libmenu, libmenuw, libpanel and libpanelw) and the programs in ncurses-bin (clear, infocmp, tabs, tic, toe, tput and tset) and ncurses-examples are dynamically linked ELF files that list the system libc.so.6 in NEEDED, and the programs name the system dynamic loader (ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 or ld-linux-aarch64.so.1) as their interpreter. libncurses-dev ships twelve static archives (libncurses.a, libncursesw.a, libtinfo.a, libtic.a, libform.a, libformw.a, libmenu.a, libmenuw.a, libpanel.a, libpanelw.a, libncurses++.a and libncurses++w.a, plus libcurses.a and libtermcap.a as symlinks to two of them) whose members are ncurses's own object files; a program that links them statically takes its C library from its own build, not from this package. The debug-symbol packages hold detached debug information, and ncurses-base, ncurses-term and ncurses-doc hold terminfo entries, tab-set files and documentation with no ELF files or archives. glibc reaches an image through the separate libc6 package, which is not part of this owner and is assessed on its own.
